response.answer: To test partial scalar invariance, use multigroup confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and align items across bilingual measures. Report results with fit indices and invariance tests. Sample size should be large enough for robust analysis.

results.title: Validation of the General Intellectual Humility Scale in French
results.content: In Study 4, we aimed to investigate the convergent validity of the French GIHS by testing whether the GIHS positively correlates with another intellectual humility scale. In this study, we tested the measurement invariance of the GIHS (i.e., the measure of intellectual humility), that is whether the psychometric properties of the scale are invariant across French and English speakers. In other words, this work provides initial evidence that the French version of the GIHS is a validated unidimensional scale measuring intellectual humility and sets the stage for further research. The first of these limitations is that we chose the related constructs based on the original scale validation work (Leary et al., 2017) and based on the possibilities of comparison with the other intellectual humility measure (e.g., unidimensionality), but for some of these constructs, we lacked validated French versions of the scales (i.e., Need for evidence, Dogmatism, Need for closure, and the PSIHS).
